raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Extend `RouterReplay.set_target_indices(..., replay_mask=None)` with an optional per-token mask. Valid rows replay rollout expert IDs; other rows retain native top-k (including group-limited selection). Return gathered current scores so router gradients remain intact. Cache the **resolved forward routes**, including native rows, for backward recomputation instead of making a second routing decision.

Omitting the mask preserves full replay. Per-microbatch masks follow the existing FIFO queue, clear with indices, and invalid/missing input fails explicitly.

## Issue tracking

Related to #8672 and [verl Modern Megatron integration RFC](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8324). Builds on the existing native R3 replay API; this does not duplicate #4256 or the experimental/lite work in #7050.

## Validation

- Slurm **H100, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, TE 2.15.0**, current Core source: **8 passed** via `torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node=1`, isolated `--noconftest --import-mode=importlib`.
- Covers mixed/full/native masks, score gradients, FIFO and clear/error behavior, and recomputation with changed score ordering.
- Registered CPU/CUDA determinism test checks exact expert IDs, values and independently specified gradients across eight repetitions. Both CPU and CUDA cases passed on H100.
- Current Core integration on Torch 2.13.0+cpu: **50 passed, 1 CUDA skip**, including these tests and the MTP/Hybrid contracts. This is separate from the locked CUDA runtime acceptance.
- Incremental `tools/autoformat.sh`: Black/isort/Pylint/Ruff pass. Nonblocking mypy reports 8 errors in the touched router module; no clean type-check claim.
- Distributed model, rollout integration and performance qualification remain pending in the verl RFC.

## Code provenance

Implemented within Megatron-Core; no third-party source copied or adapted. Split from my personal integration prototype.

## Contribution process

- [x] Unit tests and documentation
- [x] CPU/CUDA bit-exact test registered in determinism manifest
- [x] Ran `tools/autoformat.sh`
- [ ] Full functional model qualification and human line review

Draft for API and implementation review. Prepared with Codex assistance; human line-review checkbox remains unchecked.

+
+
+### Per-token router replay
+
+`RouterReplay.set_target_indices(indices, replay_mask=mask)` can replay only a
+subset of tokens. `indices` has shape `[num_tokens, topk]`; each true entry of
+`mask` selects the supplied experts, while false entries use the router's native
+selection (including group-limited or hash routing). Omitting `mask` retains
+full replay. Scores remain differentiable for the selected experts.
+
+Set targets before each `REPLAY_FORWARD` call. Both replayed and natively selected
+forward routes are saved for the corresponding `REPLAY_BACKWARD` call, in FIFO
+microbatch order. Recomputation reuses these resolved indices, so unmasked rows
+do not make another routing decision. `clear_indices()` clears targets, masks,
+and pending recomputation routes; callers should clear state on failed steps.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Masked replay retains exact expert choices, values and gathered-score gradients."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.router_replay import RouterReplay, RouterReplayAction
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("device", ["cpu", "cuda"])
+def test_masked_router_replay_is_bit_exact(device):
+    """Compare repeated executions against independently specified routes and gradients."""
+    if device == "cuda" and not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA is unavailable")
+    source = torch.tensor([[0.1, 0.8, 0.4, 0.2], [0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 0.1], [0.9, 0.2, 0.6, 0.5]])
+    expected_indices = torch.tensor([[0, 2], [2, 1], [2, 3]])
+    expected_values = torch.stack(
+        [source[row, indices] for row, indices in enumerate(expected_indices)]
+    )
+    expected_grad = torch.tensor(
+        [[0.25, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0], [0.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.25, 0.5]]
+    )
+    original_instances = list(RouterReplay.global_router_replay_instances)
+
+    def native(scores, topk, **kwargs):
+        return scores.topk(topk, dim=-1)
+
+    try:
+        for _ in range(8):
+            replay = RouterReplay()
+            scores = source.to(device).clone().requires_grad_()
+            replay.set_target_indices(
+                torch.tensor([[0, 2], [0, 3], [2, 3]], device=device),
+                torch.tensor([True, False, True], device=device),
+            )
+            replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_FORWARD)
+            values, indices = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 2, default_compute_topk=native)
+            (values * torch.tensor([0.25, 0.5], device=device)).sum().backward()
+            assert torch.equal(indices.cpu(), expected_indices)
+            assert torch.equal(values.cpu(), expected_values)
+            assert torch.equal(scores.grad.cpu(), expected_grad)
+            replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_BACKWARD)
+            recomputed_values, recomputed_indices = replay.get_replay_topk(
+                -scores.detach(), 2, default_compute_topk=native
+            )
+            assert torch.equal(recomputed_indices.cpu(), expected_indices)
+            assert torch.equal(recomputed_values.cpu(), -expected_values)
+    finally:
+        RouterReplay.global_router_replay_instances[:] = original_instances

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Per-token replay and recomputation use the same selected experts and gradients."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.router_replay import RouterReplay, RouterReplayAction
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def restore_router_registry():
+    """Keep these isolated tests from changing other models' router registries."""
+    instances = list(RouterReplay.global_router_replay_instances)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        RouterReplay.global_router_replay_instances[:] = instances
+
+
+def topk(scores, k, num_groups=None, group_topk=None):
+    return scores.topk(k, dim=-1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mask", [None, [True, False, True], [False, False, False]])
+def test_masked_replay_preserves_scores_and_gradients(mask):
+    scores = torch.tensor([[0.1, 0.8, 0.4], [0.9, 0.2, 0.5], [0.3, 0.7, 0.6]], requires_grad=True)
+    target = torch.tensor([[0, 2], [1, 2], [0, 1]], dtype=torch.int16)
+    replay = RouterReplay()
+    replay.set_target_indices(target, replay_mask=None if mask is None else torch.tensor(mask))
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_FORWARD)
+    values, indices = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 2, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    expected = target.long()
+    if mask is not None:
+        expected = torch.where(torch.tensor(mask).unsqueeze(-1), expected, scores.topk(2).indices)
+    assert torch.equal(indices, expected)
+    values.sum().backward()
+    expected_grad = torch.zeros_like(scores).scatter_(1, expected, 1)
+    assert torch.equal(scores.grad, expected_grad)
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_BACKWARD)
+    recomputed, recomputed_indices = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 2, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    assert torch.equal(recomputed_indices, indices)
+    assert torch.equal(recomputed, values)
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="no recorded microbatch"):
+        replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 2, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    replay.clear_indices()
+    assert replay.target_replay_mask is None
+    assert not replay.replay_backward_mask_list
+
+
+def test_recompute_consumes_each_microbatch_mask_in_order():
+    replay = RouterReplay()
+    scores = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [3.0, 2.0, 1.0]])
+    first = torch.tensor([[0], [2]])
+    second = torch.tensor([[1], [1]])
+    replay.set_target_indices(first, torch.tensor([True, False]))
+    replay.set_target_indices(second, torch.tensor([False, True]))
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_BACKWARD)
+    _, actual_first = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 1, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    _, actual_second = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 1, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    assert actual_first.tolist() == [[0], [0]]
+    assert actual_second.tolist() == [[2], [1]]
+
+
+def test_replay_errors_do_not_silently_use_native_routes():
+    replay = RouterReplay()
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_FORWARD)
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="requires target"):
+        replay.get_replay_topk(torch.randn(2, 3), 1, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    replay.set_target_indices(torch.zeros(2, 1, dtype=torch.long), torch.ones(3))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="one entry per token"):
+        replay.get_replay_topk(torch.randn(2, 3), 1, default_compute_topk=topk)
+
+
+def test_backward_reuses_native_rows_selected_by_forward():
+    """Unmasked forward choices must survive a different recomputation score order."""
+    replay = RouterReplay()
+    scores = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [3.0, 2.0, 1.0]])
+    replay.set_target_indices(torch.tensor([[0], [2]]), torch.tensor([True, False]))
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_FORWARD)
+    _, selected = replay.get_replay_topk(scores, 1, default_compute_topk=topk)
+    replay.set_router_replay_action(RouterReplayAction.REPLAY_BACKWARD)
+
+    def forbidden(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise AssertionError("Backward must reuse resolved forward routes.")
+
+    values, recomputed = replay.get_replay_topk(-scores, 1, default_compute_topk=forbidden)
+    assert torch.equal(selected, recomputed)
+    assert values.tolist() == [[-1.0], [-3.0]]
